trials.key_findings: Phase 2 showed up to 19% body weight loss at 46 weeks. Also showed significant liver fat reduction for MASH.
trials.efficacy_vs_semaglutide: Potentially superior for MASH due to glucagon component

trials.key_findings: ATTAIN-1 Phase 3: 27.3 lbs average weight loss at 72 weeks. No food/water restrictions — major advantage over oral semaglutide. ACHIEVE-3: superior A1C and weight outcomes vs oral semaglutide (Lancet, Feb 2026). Self-pay $149/month; $25/month commercial insurance; $50/month Medicare Part D from July 2026.
trials.efficacy_vs_semaglutide: Similar weight loss efficacy to semaglutide with significantly better convenience (no fasting requirement). Cheaper self-pay than Wegovy at $149/mo.

trials.mechanism: Semaglutide 2.4mg + cagrilintide 2.4mg (amylin analog) co-formulation — weekly injectable
trials.key_findings: REDEFINE-1: 20.4% weight loss vs 3% placebo at 68 weeks (strong). REDEFINE-4: 23% at 84 weeks but FAILED non-inferiority vs tirzepatide 15mg — key setback. NDA filed Dec 18, 2025. FDA decision expected H2 2026. Would be first GLP-1/amylin combination if approved.
trials.efficacy_vs_semaglutide: Exceeds semaglutide monotherapy (20.4% vs ~15%) but does NOT match tirzepatide 15mg — undermines commercial differentiation vs Mounjaro/Zepbound

trials.indication: Obesity, T2DM, osteoarthritis, sleep apnea, MASH
trials.mechanism: GLP-1/GIP/Glucagon triple agonist — once weekly injectable
trials.key_findings: TRIUMPH-4 Phase 3 CONFIRMED: 28.7% weight loss at 68 weeks (12mg dose) + 75.8% WOMAC knee pain reduction in obesity + osteoarthritis patients. Average 71.2 lbs lost. 1-in-8 patients completely free from knee pain at end of trial. New safety signal: 18.2% discontinuation due to AEs at high dose. 7 more Phase 3 readouts expected in 2026 (obesity, T2DM, sleep apnea, MASH, cardiovascular outcomes, back pain).
trials.efficacy_vs_semaglutide: Substantially superior: 28.7% vs ~15% weight loss. First drug to potentially break 30% weight loss in Phase 3. Safety/tolerability tradeoff vs semaglutide at high doses.

trials.key_findings: Phase 2 in Chinese population showed 16.8% weight loss at 24 weeks with biweekly dosing.
trials.efficacy_vs_semaglutide: Comparable efficacy with less frequent dosing (biweekly vs weekly)

entries.summary: CONFERENCE-DATE CORRECTION FIRST: EASD 2026 runs Sept 28 – Oct 2 in Milan, so only opening day falls in this window and every major GLP-1 readout is scheduled Sept 30 – Oct 1, OUTSIDE it — what is in-window is the pre-conference announcement layer, not the presentations. The window's real data events: Viking's VK2735 maintenance study showed every-other-week dosing retained 90% of induction weight loss versus 61% for placebo; Novo's CagriSema beat tirzepatide 5 mg on weight (12.4% vs 9.1%) but chose Lilly's second-lowest dose as comparator and disclosed no n or p-values, and shares fell ~8%; Structure's aleniglipron reached 16.2% at 72 weeks; and Novo's amycretin — now renamed zenagamtide — published two Lancet Phase 2 papers. FDA approved Mounjaro for cardiovascular risk reduction on Aug 28 on a non-inferiority result (MACE-3 HR 0.92). Zealand/Roche and AstraZeneca both launched ~7,000- and ~4,500-patient amylin Phase 3 programs.
entries.content:
August 10 - September 28, 2026 pipeline and trials.

*** CONFERENCE DATES VERIFIED AGAINST ORGANISER SITES - READ BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE ***
   - EASD 2026 (62nd): 28 SEPTEMBER - 2 OCTOBER 2026, Allianz MiCo, MILAN.
     ONLY OPENING DAY falls in this window. Every major GLP-1 readout is scheduled 30 Sept / 1 Oct -
     OUTSIDE it. Any secondary article implying TRIUMPH-2, ACHIEVE-4 or SURPASS-CVOT were 'presented'
     is describing 30 Sept-1 Oct. What IS in-window is the PRE-CONFERENCE ANNOUNCEMENT LAYER.
   - ESC Congress 2026: 28-31 AUGUST 2026, Messe Munchen, MUNICH. IN WINDOW.
   - No obesity-specific meeting in window (ECO was May; ObesityWeek is November).

1. VIKING VK2735 MAINTENANCE - THE WINDOW'S CLEANEST DATASET (Sep 22, TOPLINE PR)
   VK2735-102, Phase 2b randomised double-blind placebo-controlled, ~180 adults with obesity (BMI >=30).
   - 21-week weekly subcutaneous INDUCTION: -16.3% (15 mg), -17.8% (17.5 mg), -18.7% (20 mg),
     -17.1% (22.5 mg) vs -0.1% placebo, ALL p<0.0001
   - 12-week MAINTENANCE: pooled EVERY-OTHER-WEEK arms (n=37) retained 90% of induction weight loss;
     pooled MONTHLY arms (n=65) retained 85%; placebo (n=27) retained 61%. p<0.0001
   - AE-driven discontinuation 1% in induction, 2-3% in maintenance; maintenance GI rates not
     meaningfully different from placebo
   *** PUBLICATION CAVEAT: the 'up to 97%' headline is a SINGLE ARM OF n=12, and 'up to 90%' monthly is
   n=11. The POOLED 90%/85% figures are what this dashboard uses. The release is internally
   inconsistent on monthly n (65 in text, 66 in a table). ***
   - Viking priced an upsized $500M equity + convertible offering two days later (2026-09-24)

2. NOVO CAGRISEMA BEATS TIRZEPATIDE - ON TIRZEPATIDE'S SECOND-LOWEST DOSE (Sep 21, TOPLINE PR at CMD)
   - REIMAGINE 5, Phase 3, ~1,000 adults with T2D inadequately controlled on metformin/SGLT2i.
     CagriSema 1.0/1.0 mg vs TIRZEPATIDE 5 MG: weight loss 12.4% vs 9.1% (superior);
     HbA1c -1.71% vs -1.67% (non-inferior)
   - REDEFINE 9, Phase 3, 68 weeks, CagriSema 1.0/1.0 and 1.7/1.7 vs placebo in overweight/obesity:
     21.0% vs 2.0% for the 1.0/1.0 arm, co-primaries met
   *** NOVO DISCLOSED NO n, NO p-VALUES, NO AE OR DISCONTINUATION RATES, and DID NOT REPORT THE
   1.7/1.7 ARM. The comparator is Lilly's SECOND-LOWEST tirzepatide dose - the widely-noted weakness. ***
   - Novo shares fell ~8% on the day. CagriSema NDA filed Dec 2025; FDA decision expected Q4 2026
     (a company expectation - no public PDUFA date).

3. AMYLIN GOES BIG - TWO LARGE PHASE 3 PROGRAMS LAUNCHED IN WINDOW
   a) ZEALAND/ROCHE PETRELINTIDE - ZUPREME, ~7,000 PATIENTS (Sep 22, PROGRAM-INITIATION PR, NO NEW DATA)
      Three once-weekly subcutaneous placebo-controlled trials: ZUPREME-3 (overweight/obesity + >=1
      comorbidity, no T2D; ~3,900), ZUPREME-4 (obesity + T2D; ~600), ZUPREME-5 (obesity + established
      CVD; ~2,500). Common primary endpoint: percent body-weight change to week 64.
      *** The release cites Phase 2 ONLY QUALITATIVELY ('double-digit weight loss') - NO percentages or
      p-values. None should be attributed. Registry records for ZUPREME-3/4/5 were not yet posted. ***
   b) ASTRAZENECA AZD6234 = LENBELINTIDE - ~4,500 PATIENTS (registry first-posted Aug 20/25, REGISTRY
      RECORD, no press release located)
      NCT07784725 (n=2,500), NCT07784270 (n=1,500), NCT07776509 (n=500). All once-weekly subcutaneous
      placebo-controlled, all recruiting, identical primary endpoint of percent body-weight change at
      68 weeks; covering obesity without T2D, obesity with T2D, and adjunct-to-incretin use.
      - The registry provides the first hard AZD6234 = LENBELINTIDE INN mapping
      - AstraZeneca's own pipeline page still lists AZD6234 at PHASE II, i.e. it LAGS the registry
      - Also posted 2026-08-20: ELECOGLIPRON oral GLP-1 Phase 3 in Asian participants (n=351, NCT07775404)

4. STRUCTURE THERAPEUTICS - 16.2% AT 72 WEEKS, PLUS FIRST ORAL SMALL-MOLECULE AMYLIN DATA (Sep 8, TOPLINE PR)
   - ACCESS OLE, prespecified 36-week extension of Phase 2b ACCESS (87% of completers enrolled).
     72-week mean weight loss: 16.2% (120 mg), 14.4% (90 mg), 11.6% (45 mg), 9.0% placebo-crossover.
     <5% AE discontinuation; no drug-induced liver injury; NO p-VALUES REPORTED.
   - ACCG-2671 (oral small-molecule amylin) Phase 1/2a SAD, 31 healthy adults: 3.3% mean weight
     reduction at Day 24 from a SINGLE 10 mg dose (n=6), ~6-day half-life, no SAEs, but DOSE-DEPENDENT
     EMESIS - absent at <=2 mg, 4 of 5 at 5 mg, 6 of 6 at 10 mg.

5. NOVO AMYCRETIN RENAMED ZENAGAMTIDE - TWO LANCET PHASE 2 PAPERS (Aug 15, PEER-REVIEWED PUBLICATION)
   36-week Phase 2 dose-finding, 83 sites / 11 countries (NCT06542874).
   - SUBCUTANEOUS (n=225 drug, 37 placebo): HbA1c -0.9% at 0.4 mg (ETD -0.77%, 95% CI -1.26 to -0.28,
     p=0.0021) through -1.7% at 40 mg (ETD -1.56%, -2.05 to -1.07, p<0.0001); SAEs 21/261 (8%); no deaths
   - ORAL (n=156 drug, 30 placebo): -0.9% at 6 mg (ETD -0.5%, p=0.033), -1.3% at 25 mg (p=0.0001),
     -1.4% at 50 mg (ETD -1.09%, p<0.0001); GI AEs 26%/41%/47% by ascending dose vs 23% placebo;
     SAEs 7/186 (4%); no deaths
   - NAMING: amycretin -> ZENAGAMTIDE. Dashboard already carries the zenagamtide name; noted for consistency.

6. LILLY PRE-EASD RELEASE - ACHIEVE-4 CVOT NUMBERS, BUT NOT SUPERIORITY (Sep 15, PRE-CONFERENCE ANNOUNCEMENT)
   Full presentations 30 Sept-1 Oct, OUT OF WINDOW.
   - ACHIEVE-4: orforglipron (Foundayo) NON-INFERIOR to insulin glargine; 16% lower MACE-4
     (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.59-1.20) and 23% lower MACE-3 (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.52-1.13)
     *** BOTH CONFIDENCE INTERVALS CROSS 1.0 - SUPERIORITY WAS NOT DEMONSTRATED. ***
   - Recapped: retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 up to 22.5 kg / 20.8% weight loss and up to -1.6% A1C at 80 weeks;
     SURPASS-CVOT MACE-3 HR 0.92 (95.3% CI 0.83-1.01); eloraTZP Phase 1 - eloralintide 3 mg +
     tirzepatide 5 mg gave 17% weight loss at 16 weeks vs 10% with tirzepatide alone
   - No n, p-values, AE or discontinuation rates in the release

7. FDA APPROVES MOUNJARO FOR CARDIOVASCULAR RISK REDUCTION (Aug 28, REGULATORY APPROVAL - LABEL EXPANSION)
   - New indication: reduce CV death, non-fatal MI or non-fatal stroke in adults with T2D at high risk
   - Based on SURPASS-CVOT, the FIRST HEAD-TO-HEAD INCRETIN CVOT: tirzepatide vs dulaglutide,
     >13,000 participants, 30 countries, median ~4 years follow-up
   - MACE-3 HR 0.92 (95.3% CI 0.83-1.01)
   *** THIS IS A NON-INFERIORITY RESULT, NOT SUPERIORITY. The CI crosses 1.0. ***

8. MHRA AUTHORISES ORFORGLIPRON - UK FIRST IN EUROPE (Aug 10, REGULATORY APPROVAL)
   Once-daily oral non-peptide GLP-1 for weight management and T2D glycaemic control. Titration
   0.8 -> 2.5 -> 5.5 -> 9 -> 14.5 -> 17.2 mg, minimum one month per step. Most common AEs: nausea,
   constipation, diarrhoea, vomiting, dyspepsia, abdominal pain. Prescription-only and NOT NHS-FUNDED
   pending NICE appraisal - a material commercial constraint. (FDA approval was 2026-04-01, out of window.)
   Cross-referenced in reg-entry-022.

9. STEP 12 - SEMAGLUTIDE AT LOWER ASIAN BMI THRESHOLDS (Aug 10 online, PEER-REVIEWED, Lancet D&E)
   Phase 3b, 19 sites mainland China and Taiwan, 242 adults randomised 2:1 at locally-defined BMI
   thresholds (24-<28 with comorbidity, or 28-<30), 44 weeks (NCT06041217).
   - Weight change -12.1% vs -2.2% placebo (ETD -9.9 pp, 95% CI -11.8 to -8.0, p<0.0001)
   - >=5% weight loss in 80.5% vs 24.4% (OR 14.8, 7.4-29.6, p<0.0001)
   - AEs 87.6% vs 75.3%, predominantly GI

10. A GENUINELY NEW INDICATION - GLP-1/GIP INTO HIDRADENITIS SUPPURATIVA (registry Sep 21, REGISTRY RECORD)
   NCT07830329. Phase 2, randomised double-blind placebo-controlled, 52 weeks, 300 adults with
   moderate-to-severe hidradenitis suppurativa AND overweight/obesity. Drug is OLATOREPATIDE, registry
   otherName HS-20094 (Hansoh), run by Regeneron. Primary endpoint is percent change in total abscess
   and inflammatory-nodule count at week 52 - NOT weight. Clearest in-window signal of a
   Chinese-originated obesity asset being pushed into an inflammatory indication by a US partner.

11. ESC 2026 GUIDELINES ADD GLP-1s FOR HFpEF WITH OBESITY (presented Aug 29 Munich; EHJ advance ~Sep 1)
   For the first time, semaglutide or tirzepatide 'should be considered' in symptomatic HF with
   LVEF >=45% and BMI >=30 kg/m2, REGARDLESS OF DIABETES STATUS, to reduce weight and improve exercise
   capacity and quality of life.
   *** FLAG: secondary sources CONFLICT on the recommendation class (IIa vs IIb) and none stated the
   level of evidence. The class could NOT be verified from the guideline text itself. NO CLASS IS
   PUBLISHED HERE. Check the EHJ document before asserting one. ***

12. CHINESE PIPELINE - PROGRESS, BUT NO NEW OUT-LICENSING DEAL
   - HENGRUI HRS-7535 (oral small-molecule GLP-1, = Kailera KAI-7535): met ALL primary and key secondary
     endpoints at Week 44 in a China Phase III obesity study, weight loss continuing through Week 50,
     mean body-weight reduction UP TO 11.1%; NDA submission planned. Kailera's own disclosure puts
     HARBOR-1 at 11.1% mean weight loss at Week 50 (180 mg) - CONSISTENT.
     *** SOURCING: disclosed inside Hengrui's 2026 INTERIM RESULTS (Aug 19), NOT a standalone topline PR
     and NOT a conference presentation. No n, dose arms, comparator, p-values, AE or discontinuation
     rates were disclosed - none are supplied here. ***
   - RIBUPATIDE (HRS9531, GLP-1/GIP dual): two China Phase III studies in T2D reported positive topline,
     NDA submission planned. Same sourcing caveat.
   - INNOVENT: 2026 interim results describe mazdutide as the world's first approved GCG/GLP-1 dual
     agonist for obesity and T2D but disclose NO sales figure, NO new readout, NO new NMPA filing and NO
     out-licensing deal. Next-gen pipeline listed as IBI3032, IBI3042, IBI3040, IBI3046, IBI3030.
     IBI3016 was NOT mentioned - nothing verified on it.
   - *** NO NEW CHINESE OBESITY OUT-LICENSING DEAL WAS CONFIRMED IN WINDOW. The Pfizer/Sciwind $495M,
     Pfizer/YaoPharma and AZ/CSPC deals are ALL PRE-WINDOW (Jan-Feb 2026) and must not be dated into it.
     The Lilly-InnoCare deal (~Sep 24, $100M upfront + up to $3.25B) is ONCOLOGY/AUTOIMMUNE, not obesity. ***
   - UNVERIFIED: a reported $9M Novo milestone payment to United Laboratories on UBT251 (2026-09-24).
     This would be a milestone under the existing March 2025 licence, NOT a new deal. Figure, trigger and
     territory all unverified. NOT published as fact.

13. MID-CAP AND MUSCLE-PRESERVATION - TWO FDA APPROVALS IN THE MYOSTATIN/ACTIVIN CLASS
   - SCHOLAR ROCK: FDA approved ISEMBYLD (apitegromab-mstn) for SPINAL MUSCULAR ATROPHY on 2026-09-11
     on Phase 3 SAPPHIRE (NCT05156320, n=188, ages 2-21, 9 countries; 10 mg/kg recommended, 20 mg/kg
     also tested, IV q4w ~1 year on SMN2 background). Primary endpoint 2.2-point HFMSE improvement
     (nominal p=0.0121); 34.2% achieved >=3-point HFMSE increase vs 13.5% placebo (OR 3.8, nominal
     p=0.0125). Fractures 9% on 10 mg/kg vs 2% placebo; 98% continued into the ONYX extension.
     THIS IS THE SMA INDICATION - the release contains NO EMBRAZE/obesity data.
     *** MATERIALLY RELEVANT CORRECTION: on 2026-09-15 Scholar Rock filed a Reg-FD 8-K CORRECTING
     statements from its Sept 14 investor call. Management had incorrectly said FDA required no
     post-marketing safety commitments on bone or reproductive safety. FDA IN FACT REQUIRED (1) a
     pregnancy safety study collecting pregnancy complications and birth outcomes, and (2) submission of
     serious and non-serious domestic and foreign FRACTURE cases as 15-day alert reports. FDA is
     actively policing fracture and reproductive safety for this class - directly relevant to the
     obesity muscle-preservation thesis. ***
   - REGENERON: FDA approved PASATRU (garetosmab-grts, anti-activin A) for FIBRODYSPLASIA OSSIFICANS
     PROGRESSIVA on 2026-08-19. Garetosmab is the third agent in Regeneron's COURAGE triplet, so it now
     carries an approved-drug safety database. *** The press-release BODY could not be retrieved
     (JS-rendered, WebFetch timeout): NO trial name, n, dose, endpoint numbers, p-values, AE or
     discontinuation rates are available and none are guessed here. ***
   - ALTIMMUNE: PERFORMA global Phase 3 in non-cirrhotic MASH INITIATED August 2026 (registry
     NCT07795164, n=1,800), 52-week data anticipated 2029; $519M cash at Jun 30 2026. The PERFORMA
     initiation PR (2026-08-03) and RECLAIM AUD topline (2026-07-28) are both OUT OF WINDOW.
   - KAILERA: Phase 2b US high-dose obesity trial (NCT07458269, n=264, BMI >=35 without T2D,
     10/13/16/20 mg once-weekly, 48 weeks) FULLY ENROLLED, data mid-2027; global Phase 3 KaiNETIC-1/-2/-3
     >4,700 adults, once-weekly up to 10 mg, 76 weeks, data 2028; $1.17bn cash into mid-2028. Kailera's
     IPO 8-K was 2026-04-20, OUT OF WINDOW.
   - VERU: Phase 2b PLATEAU (enobosarm 3 mg + semaglutide, age >=65, BMI >=35) FULLY ENROLLED at n=239,
     above the ~200 previously guided. Primary endpoint percent change in total body weight at 68 weeks;
     interim Q1 CY2027, final topline Q4 2027. NO efficacy data released; NO AE or discontinuation rates.
   - NO VERIFIED IN-WINDOW NEWS: Terns (zero SEC filings across the 7-week window), BioAge,
     Pfizer/Metsera (no 8-K; newsroom not scanned, so unverified rather than confirmed absent),
     Verdiva (private), Zealand survodutide partnership (delisted, no EDGAR).

14. ALSO IN WINDOW, LOWER VALUE BUT REAL
   - Novo pre-EASD release, 44 abstracts, no numbers (Sep 16)
   - Pfizer berobenatide (ex-Metsera MET-097i) Phase 3 expansion into Japan, China and OSA (Aug 28-Sep 16)
   - New Phase 3 starts: United Labs UBT251, Huadong HDM1005, Sciwind ecnoglutide in adolescents,
     Shanghai Minwei MWN109
   - Boehringer opened a survodutide Phase 3 in T2D (n=600, registry Aug 10)
   - Dual GLP-1/glucagon agonist meta-analysis, 16 trials / 6,611 participants, -7.44% placebo-corrected
     weight (Aug 21)
   - ATTAIN-1 post hoc 10-year risk prediction (Sep 17)
   - Orforglipron menopause-stage analysis, up to 14% weight loss across all three stages, 142-225 women
     per group - *** EASD CONFERENCE ABSTRACT, NOT PEER-REVIEWED *** (Sep 26)

15. TWO THINGS WORTH WATCHING THAT ARE NOT NEWS
   - Lilly terminated LY3549492 Phase 2 'for strategic business reasons' (registry update Aug 31) - but
     ACTUAL ENROLLMENT WAS 1, so this is RECORD CLEANUP, NOT A FAILURE. Do not report as a trial halt.
   - The SURVODUTIDE CVOT (NCT06077864, n=5,531 actual) is marked COMPLETED as of 2026-06-30 with a
     2026-09-17 record update and NO TOPLINE DISCLOSED. This is the largest unreported readout sitting
     adjacent to the window. WATCH ITEM.

16. VERIFIED NEGATIVES FOR THIS WINDOW
   NO in-window news for: Amgen MariTide/MARITIME efficacy, bimagrumab + semaglutide (BELIEVE),
   Roche CT-996, or readouts in MASH, HFpEF, CKD, Alzheimer's, knee OA, PAD or addiction.

17. ROCHE ENICEPATIDE (CT-388) - BEST-IN-DISEASE PHASE 2 DIABETES DATA (Sep 22, TOPLINE PR, Art. 53 LR)
   Trial CT-388-104, Phase 2, n=447 adults with T2D and overweight/obesity, once-weekly subcutaneous,
   highest titrated dose 24 mg, placebo-controlled. Co-primaries: change from baseline in HbA1c and body
   weight at week 48.
   - 24 mg arm: mean HbA1c reduction 2.65% from baseline 8.1%; among those with baseline above 8.5% the
     reduction was 4.13%
   - Mean weight loss 15.5% at 48 weeks, described as WITHOUT A WEIGHT-LOSS PLATEAU
   - 90% of the 24 mg arm reached HbA1c <=6.5%; 62% achieved NORMOGLYCEMIA (HbA1c <5.7%)
   - AEs predominantly mild-to-moderate GI; AE-driven discontinuation 2.0% vs 0.0% placebo
   *** Roche did NOT state p-values and did NOT report the placebo arm's HbA1c or weight numbers -
   an omission several outlets noted. ***
   - Two Phase 3 weight-management studies, ENITH-1 and ENITH-2, are already running
   - A petrelintide + enicepatide Phase 2 combination is stated as planned for 2H 2026

18. ROCHE PAYS HANMI UP TO $2.3BN FOR A MUSCLE-SPARING ASSET (Aug 24, LICENSING DEAL)
   - $190 MILLION UP FRONT plus up to $2.3 BILLION in development, regulatory and commercial milestones
     plus royalties, for ex-South Korea rights to Hanmi's HM17321
   - HM17321 is a UROCORTIN-2 ANALOG designed to spur fat loss while PRESERVING LEAN MASS
   - Hanmi finishes the ongoing Phase 1 dosing study, after which Roche assumes development
   - Roche is racing Denmark's Gubra, which started a Phase 1/2 urocortin-2 trial in July 2026
   - STRATEGIC READ: a direct bet on the main clinical criticism of Zepbound and Wegovy - muscle loss
     accompanying rapid weight reduction. Sits alongside the two myostatin/activin-class FDA approvals
     in section 13 and the SMD -0.52 lean-mass meta-analysis in safety-entry-018.
   - NOTE: this deal does NOT appear in Roche's own media-release sitemap for the window; it is verified
     from BioPharma Dive and Endpoints, not from a Roche primary source.

19. STEP YOUNG - FIRST LARGE CONTROLLED PEDIATRIC READOUT IN AGES 6 TO UNDER 12 (Sep 7, TOPLINE PR)
   - Primary endpoint MET: superior BMI reduction at week 68 for once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide
     plus lifestyle modification vs placebo plus lifestyle modification
   - 40.4% OF SEMAGLUTIDE-TREATED CHILDREN WERE NO LONGER CLASSIFIED AS HAVING OBESITY AT WEEK 68,
     VERSUS 0% ON PLACEBO - two in five moved to normal-weight or overweight classification
   - More than 85% of enrolled children had CLASS II OR III SEVERE OBESITY at baseline (equivalent to
     adult BMI >=35 and >=40 respectively)
   - Safety and tolerability consistent with adult and adolescent trials
   - Significant label-expansion and public-health lever. Cross-reference: safety-entry-018 records a
     separate adolescent cohort (n=9,222 per arm) finding LOWER suicide-related events, HR 0.74.

20. AMYLYX AVEXITIDE - A GLP-1 *ANTAGONIST* WINS PHASE 3 (Aug 18, TOPLINE PR)
   - 55% REDUCTION in serious-to-severe hypoglycemic events vs placebo in post-bariatric hypoglycemia
   - Reported safe with mostly mild adverse events
   - *** MECHANISM IS THE INVERSE of the obesity blockbusters - it BLOCKS GLP-1 rather than agonising it.
     Amylyx acquired the asset cheaply out of a bankruptcy auction. ***
   - Validates GLP-1 antagonism as a commercial category, and marks a comeback for a company best known
     for its withdrawn ALS drug

21. NOVO STARTS A LOWEST-EFFECTIVE-DOSE STUDY FOR THE WEGOVY PILL (Aug 19, TRIAL INITIATION)
   - Novo initiated a study testing LOWER MAINTENANCE DOSES of oral semaglutide
   - MARGIN LOGIC: oral semaglutide consumes far more active peptide per patient than the injectable, so
     a lower effective maintenance dose is directly a cost-of-goods and capacity lever - it connects to
     the 10x oral capacity target in mfg-entry-019
   - *** Reuters returns HTTP 401 to automated fetch. The existence and date of the story are verified
     from the retrieved search index; DOSE LEVELS AND PATIENT NUMBERS ARE NOT VERIFIED and none are
     published. WSJ covered the same development Aug 19 and BioSpace Aug 21. ***

entries.summary: Retatrutide's TRIUMPH-2 and -3 readouts (Jul 23) dominated the window — 22.6% weight loss in severe obesity with established CVD, but cardiovascular EVENT reduction did not reach significance (MACE-5 HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.55–1.22; MACE-3 HR 1.12). BLA now guides to Q1 2027. Orforglipron for T2D sits in FDA 'Regulatory Review' — filed but not approved. Novo renamed amycretin to zenagamtide and published both Phase 2 formulations in The Lancet (Jul 30), with AMBITION Phase 3 to launch before year-end. Mazdutide's GLORY-2 published in JAMA at 16.65% weight loss. Two persistent negatives: CagriSema still has no public PDUFA date, and survodutide still has no NDA on file.
entries.content:
July–August 2026 pipeline:

1. ⭐ RETATRUTIDE TRIUMPH-2 & TRIUMPH-3 (Jul 23)
   - TRIUMPH-2 (NCT05929079, n=1,152, T2D+obesity, 80wk): −12.7%/−19.1%/−20.8% at 4/9/12mg vs −4.0% placebo; A1C −1.4/−1.6/−1.5% vs −0.2% (baseline 7.7%); AE discontinuation 3.8/11.6/7.7% vs 4.9%
   - TRIUMPH-3 (NCT05882045, n=1,949, BMI ≥35 + established CVD, 80wk): −21.6% (9mg), −22.6% (12mg, −55.8 lbs) vs −3.2% placebo
   - Risk factors moved hard: triglycerides −37.0%, non-HDL-C −16.5%, SBP −9.3 mmHg, waist −7.5 in, hsCRP −51.2%
   - ⚠️ CV EVENTS DID NOT REACH SIGNIFICANCE: MACE-5 HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.55–1.22; 44 vs 52 events); MACE-3 HR 1.12 (0.64–1.96; 27 vs 23)
   - AE discontinuation 9.8%/13.5% vs 4.8%; diarrhea up to 33.6%, nausea up to 28.0%
   - BLA guides Q1 2027 via the biologics pathway — a slip from prior Q4 2026 expectations; reaffirmed at Q2 earnings
   - Five positive Phase 3 studies now in hand

2. ORFORGLIPRON (FOUNDAYO)
   - T2D indication listed as 'Regulatory Review' on Lilly's pipeline page as of Aug 5 — submitted with a National Priority Review Voucher, NOT yet approved
   - ACHIEVE-5 published JAMA Aug 4 (NCT06109311, n=546, insulin add-on): A1C −1.58/−1.88/−1.82% at 3/12/36mg vs −0.79% placebo; weight −2.6/−4.8/−5.4% vs +0.2%; no increased hypoglycemia
   - Obesity indication remains Phase 3 across CV outcomes, hypertension, OSA, OA pain, PAD, stress urinary incontinence
   - 'First Approval' monograph (Jul 21) notes submissions pending in EU, Japan, Canada

3. NOVO — ZENAGAMTIDE (renamed from amycretin)
   - Both Phase 2 formulations published simultaneously in The Lancet, Jul 30 (NCT06542874, T2D, 36wk)
   - Subcutaneous (n=262): A1C −0.77% at 0.4mg to −1.56% at 40mg; 8% serious AEs
   - Oral (n=186): A1C −0.5/−0.99/−1.09% at 6/25/50mg; GI AEs 26–47% vs 23% placebo
   - AMBITION Phase 3 programme to launch before year-end

4. CAGRISEMA — STILL NO PUBLIC PDUFA
   - Novo reaffirmed only 'US regulatory decision end-2026 with potential 2027 launch' at Q2
   - REDEFINE 9 completed (68wk, lower maintenance doses 1.0/1.7mg each component) — superior weight loss vs placebo
   - NEW Phase IIIb initiated: higher fixed-dose CagriSema (cagrilintide 2.4mg + semaglutide 7.2mg) vs CagriSema 2.4/2.4 and vs semaglutide 7.2mg alone
   - REDEFINE 1 post hoc (Jul 26): 30.3% of CagriSema patients reached BMI <27 AND WHtR <0.53 at wk 68 vs 19.1% semaglutide

5. SURVODUTIDE — STILL UNFILED
   - No NDA/BLA as of August 2026
   - Phase 2 MASH mediation analysis (Hepatology, Aug 3, n=170): fibrosis improvement only 36.3% mediated by weight loss — supports a direct hepatic effect of glucagon agonism independent of weight

6. OTHER PHASE 3 ENTRANTS
   - Mazdutide GLORY-2 (JAMA, Aug 4; NCT06163873, n=461 Chinese adults): −16.65% vs −1.50% placebo at 60wk; 84.3% achieved ≥5%; AE discontinuation only 2.9% but vomiting 53.1%, nausea 46.9%
   - Ecnoglutide: FIRST APPROVALS in China for T2D glycemic control (Jul 7)
   - Zalfermin + semaglutide Phase 2 MASH (Lancet Gastro Hep, Jul 15, n=698): combo MISSED (24% vs 16% placebo, p=0.19); semaglutide 2.4mg alone nominally positive (30%, p=0.024)
   - Early stage: HRS-7535 Phase 2 DKD (Jul 9), TERN-601 Phase 1/2 (Jul 30)

7. ADJACENT — NOVO'S ZILTIVEKIMAB FAILS ZEUS (Jul 31)
   - Anti-IL-6, NOT a GLP-1. Missed MACE primary in >6,300 patients, HR 0.99, despite target engagement
   - Novo shares fell ~9%; materially reshaped Novo's cardiometabolic narrative

8. ⚠️ REPUBLICATION TRAP
   - CagriSema REIMAGINE 1/2/3, orforglipron ACHIEVE-2, survodutide SYNCHRONIZE-JP all carry Jul/Aug print dates but were published online Jun 7–8 (ADA-adjacent). NOT new news.

9. PIPELINE NEGATIVES (verified)
   - Petrelintide: no Phase 3 initiation announced; ZUPREME still guided H2 2026
   - Eloralintide: no new readout; Phase 3 ongoing
   - Berobenatide (Pfizer): no news; first late-stage data guided H2 2027. Pfizer separately DISCONTINUED an ex-Metsera GLP-1 and a GIPR prospect in its Q2 clearout
   - Elecoglipron (AZ): no news; EMBOLD Phase 3 announced pre-window
   - TRIUMPH-1 and TRIUMPH-5: no new disclosures
   - No major obesity/diabetes congress fell in this window (ADA was Jun 5–8)

entries.content:
ADA 2026 — Boehringer survodutide SYNCHRONIZE detailed readout:

1. SYNCHRONIZE-1 (PRIMARY, OBESITY):
   - 16.6% weight loss vs 3.2% placebo at 76 weeks (p<0.0001)
   - 85.1% achieved ≥5% loss
   - 34% visceral adipose tissue reduction (CT-measured)
   - 63.1% hepatic fat reduction (MRI-PDFF)

2. SYNCHRONIZE-MASLD SUBGROUP:
   - 84.2% achieved ≥30% liver fat reduction vs 24.3% placebo
   - 12.2% weight loss vs 1.0% placebo
   - Validates glucagon-mechanism MASLD hypothesis

3. LEAN MASS PRESERVATION:
   - 10.8% of total tissue change is lean mass
   - Better than typical 25-40% lean-mass loss with sema/tirz
   - Glucagon receptor agonism preserves muscle via energy expenditure

4. TOLERABILITY CONCERN:
   - **19% GI-related discontinuation rate** — substantially higher than survodutide P2 (8-10%) and tirzepatide (~12%)
   - Could limit broad adoption despite efficacy/liver advantages

5. MASH PHASE 3 PENDING:
   - LIVERAGE (non-cirrhotic): readout 2027
   - LIVERAGE-Cirrhosis: readout 2027-2028
   - If positive, survodutide would be first dual-mechanism MASH therapy

6. COMPETITIVE POSITIONING:
   - 16.6% obesity weight loss: below tirzepatide (~22%), retatrutide (~28%), CagriSema (~14.2%)
   - But: best-in-class MASLD/MASH efficacy + lean mass preservation
   - Niche play: high-CV/CKD-risk + metabolic dysfunction-associated liver disease patients

7. REGULATORY OUTLOOK:
   - NDA filing target Q4 2026 / early 2027
   - FDA decision target 2028
   - Boehringer + Zealand Pharma royalty arrangement

entries.content:
April 28, 2026 — Boehringer Ingelheim announced positive Phase 3 SYNCHRONIZE-1 results for survodutide:

1. SYNCHRONIZE-1 PRIMARY RESULTS:
   - 16.6% mean weight loss (high dose) vs 3.2% placebo at 76 weeks

   - First Phase 3 obesity readout for a glucagon-containing dual agonist
   - Full data presentation at ADA 2026 Scientific Sessions (June 5-8, New Orleans)

   - Tirzepatide (Lilly): GLP-1 + GIP dual agonist (~21% weight loss in SURMOUNT)
   - Retatrutide (Lilly): GLP-1 + GIP + glucagon triple agonist (~28.7% weight loss in TRIUMPH-4)
   - Survodutide's lower weight-loss numbers vs tirzepatide/retatrutide may be offset by metabolic improvements (BP, lipids, A1c, hepatic fat) attributable to glucagon mechanism.

3. MASH OPPORTUNITY:
   - Survodutide's glucagon agonism drives stronger energy expenditure and hepatic fat reduction
   - Phase 3 MASH trials: LIVERAGE (non-cirrhotic) and LIVERAGE-Cirrhosis (cirrhotic)
   - MASH represents a large unmet need where current GLP-1 monotherapy has not been broadly successful
   - If LIVERAGE trials read out positive, survodutide could be the first dual-mechanism therapy for liver disease

   - Boehringer + Zealand Pharma partnership (royalties to Zealand)
   - NDA filing expected Q4 2026 / early 2027 if trial pattern holds

   - Differentiation: lower discontinuation rate than retatrutide (8-10% vs 18.2% at high dose)

5. RECEPTOR-LEVEL CONTEXT:
   - Industry now has at least 4 distinct mechanisms: GLP-1 monotherapy (semaglutide), GIP/GLP-1 dual (tirzepatide), GLP-1/glucagon dual (survodutide, mazdutide), GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple (retatrutide)

entries.content:
April 2026 GLP-1 pipeline summary:

1. RETATRUTIDE TRIUMPH-4 CONFIRMED (Eli Lilly): The first Phase 3 data for retatrutide (GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist) arrived in April 2026. TRIUMPH-4 in patients with obesity + knee osteoarthritis: 28.7% mean body weight reduction at 68 weeks on 12mg dose (equivalent to 71.2 lbs). WOMAC pain scores fell 75.8%. 1-in-8 patients fully pain-free at trial end. Safety note: 18.2% discontinuation rate from adverse events — higher than semaglutide or tirzepatide. Seven more Phase 3 trials (TRIUMPH-1 through 7) expected to read out in 2026. NDA filing target Q4 2026. FDA decision 2027-2028. GlobalData 2031 sales forecast: $15.6 billion.

2. CAGRISEMA NDA REVIEW (Novo Nordisk): Novo filed NDA December 18, 2025 for CagriSema (semaglutide 2.4mg + cagrilintide 2.4mg, once-weekly injectable). REDEFINE-1 trial: 20.4% weight loss vs 3% placebo at 68 weeks — strong absolute result. However, REDEFINE-4 at 84 weeks achieved 23% weight loss but MISSED non-inferiority vs tirzepatide 15mg — the primary endpoint. This miss is commercially significant: it removes the key differentiation argument vs Mounjaro/Zepbound. FDA PDUFA expected H2 2026. If approved, CagriSema is the first GLP-1/amylin combination on market — a mechanistically novel approach.

3. FOUNDAYO APPROVED & LAUNCHED (Eli Lilly): See story-029 for details. Pipeline → Approved. Market available from April 6 via LillyDirect, Amazon Pharmacy, and retail. First non-peptide oral GLP-1 RA with no food/water restrictions. Self-pay $149/mo, Medicare $50/mo from July 2026.

4. MFN DEAL IMPACT ON PIPELINE ECONOMICS: The Trump MFN deal ($245/mo government price, $50 patient copay from July 2026 under Medicare) changes the commercial landscape for all pipeline GLP-1s. Drugs entering market 2027-2029 will likely face immediate MFN pricing pressure if they seek Medicare/Medicaid formulary access. This compresses the expected peak sales for retatrutide and CagriSema relative to pre-MFN forecasts.

entries.summary: ACC 2026 / JAMA Cardiology: Tirzepatide reduced a 6-point cardiorenal composite endpoint by 16% vs dulaglutide (23.7% vs 27.4%) in 13,000+ T2DM + CVD patients over ~4 years (SURPASS-CVOT post hoc). All-cause mortality HR 0.84, kidney outcomes HR 0.79.
entries.content: A post hoc analysis of the SURPASS-CVOT randomized controlled trial presented at the American College of Cardiology (ACC) 2026 Annual Scientific Sessions in New Orleans (March 28-30, 2026) and simultaneously published in JAMA Cardiology provides the most comprehensive cardiorenal evidence to date for tirzepatide versus a GLP-1 monotherapy comparator. The analysis included 13,076 patients with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease followed for a median of 3.7 years. Tirzepatide reduced the primary 6-point composite cardiorenal endpoint (cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, heart failure hospitalization, coronary revascularization, and adverse kidney outcomes) by 16% vs dulaglutide (23.7% vs 27.4%; HR 0.84; 95% CI 0.78-0.91; p<0.0001). Component outcomes: all-cause mortality HR 0.84 (p=0.005), coronary revascularization HR 0.84 (p=0.001), adverse kidney outcomes HR 0.79 (p=0.001). The 3-point MACE endpoint (CV death, MI, stroke) was numerically but not statistically significantly different (HR 0.94; p=0.27). Gastrointestinal adverse events were more common with tirzepatide (42.5% vs 35.9%). This is a post hoc analysis of a trial designed to compare tirzepatide vs dulaglutide — not a prespecified superiority test — but the cardiorenal composite finding is robust and consistent across subgroups. Key implication: dual GIP/GLP-1 agonism appears to confer meaningful cardiorenal protection over GLP-1 monotherapy, supporting tirzepatide (and future triple agonists) as the preferred agent in high-CV/CKD-risk patients. Funded by Eli Lilly.

entries.summary: Retatrutide (Lilly's triple agonist) scored a 'triple trial triumph' with 26-28.7% weight loss in Phase 3 TRIUMPH-4, but a new safety signal emerged: 18.2% of patients on the high dose discontinued due to adverse events. Seven more Phase 3 readouts expected in 2026 across obesity, sleep apnea, osteoarthritis, back pain, and liver disease.
entries.content: Eli Lilly's retatrutide (GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist) achieved an extraordinary Phase 3 milestone in TRIUMPH-4, delivering 28.7% weight loss on-treatment (23.7% treatment-regimen) at 68 weeks with the 12mg dose — the highest ever reported for a pharmaceutical agent in any late-stage obesity trial. The trial also demonstrated approximately 75% pain reduction in knee osteoarthritis patients, significantly expanding the drug's potential beyond metabolic disease. However, BioSpace reporting highlights a new safety signal that emerged at scale: 18.2% of patients on the high dose discontinued due to adverse events (nausea 43.2%, diarrhea 33.1%), a considerably higher discontinuation rate than seen with semaglutide (approximately 10-12%) or tirzepatide. This tolerability question is the central debate among analysts assessing retatrutide's commercial potential vs its efficacy advantage. Seven more Phase 3 readouts are expected in 2026 covering obesity (TRIUMPH-1, with 80-week data potentially showing >30% weight loss), type 2 diabetes (TRANSCEND-T2D-1 already reported 16.8% weight loss), sleep apnea, chronic low back pain, cardiovascular outcomes, and MASH. GlobalData predicts a 2027 approval, with 2031 sales forecasted at $15.6 billion. Citi analysts expect TRIUMPH-1 to specifically hit the 30% weight loss threshold given its 80-week trial length.

entries.summary: Orforglipron (Lilly's oral non-peptide GLP-1) has now beaten semaglutide in a head-to-head Type 2 diabetes Phase 3 trial, strengthening its FDA approval case. FDA decision expected Q2 2026 under National Priority Review. If approved, it will be the first oral non-peptide GLP-1 and self-pay pricing is set at $149-399/month — directly challenging injectable market economics.
entries.content: Eli Lilly's orforglipron has achieved a significant clinical milestone that changes the competitive calculus: in a Phase 3 head-to-head trial (ACHIEVE), orforglipron demonstrated superior A1C reduction compared to Novo Nordisk's semaglutide in type 2 diabetes, making it the first oral GLP-1 to beat the gold-standard injectable in a direct comparison. Combined with the ATTAIN-MAINTAIN data (patients switching from injectable Wegovy maintained weight with only 0.9 kg difference), orforglipron's efficacy-to-convenience trade-off appears highly favorable. The FDA decision is expected in Q2 2026 under the National Priority Review Voucher program, which compressed the review timeline to approximately 6 months. If approved, orforglipron will be the first oral non-peptide GLP-1 agonist — distinct from Novo's oral Wegovy pill (which is still a peptide requiring food restrictions). Orforglipron can be taken without food or water restrictions, a meaningful patient convenience advantage over oral semaglutide. Self-pay pricing is expected at $149-399/month, significantly below the $936-$1,349 range for injectable competitors. Truist Securities estimates Lilly's three-drug incretin franchise (Mounjaro, Zepbound, orforglipron) could reach $101 billion at peak sales, with orforglipron's oral convenience potentially unlocking a previously untapped segment of injection-averse patients. India-specific significance: injection aversion is substantially higher in India than in the US, potentially making an affordable oral GLP-1 even more disruptive in the Indian market once generic versions become available post-patent expiry.

entries.summary: Novo Nordisk's CagriSema Phase 3 REDEFINE trial topline results are expected imminently, with analyst consensus expecting weight loss in the 20-22% range.
entries.content: Novo Nordisk's CagriSema Phase 3 REDEFINE trial topline results are expected imminently, with analyst consensus expecting weight loss in the 20-22% range. The product, combining semaglutide with amylin analog cagrilintide, is positioned as Novo Nordisk's next-generation obesity treatment to maintain market leadership against tirzepatide and retatrutide.

entries.summary: Eli Lilly confirmed that enrollment is complete for the ACHIEVE Phase 3 program evaluating orforglipron, the first oral non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist.
entries.content: Eli Lilly confirmed that enrollment is complete for the ACHIEVE Phase 3 program evaluating orforglipron, the first oral non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist. If successful, orforglipron could dramatically expand the addressable GLP-1 market by eliminating the injection barrier that limits current uptake, particularly in markets like India where injection aversion is significant.

entries.summary: Orforglipron completed its third successful Phase 3 trial (ATTAIN-MAINTAIN), demonstrating that patients switching from injectable Wegovy or Zepbound could maintain weight loss on the oral pill, triggering global regulatory submissions.
entries.content: Eli Lilly's orforglipron succeeded across all three Phase 3 ATTAIN obesity trials and two ACHIEVE diabetes trials, triggering global regulatory submissions in 2025. In ATTAIN-1, the 36mg dose achieved 7.9-10.5% weight loss at 72 weeks. Critically, ATTAIN-MAINTAIN showed patients switching from injectable Wegovy maintained weight with only 0.9 kg difference, while those from Zepbound maintained with 5.0 kg difference. The oral pill, which can be taken without food or water restrictions unlike oral Wegovy, received National Priority Review Voucher designation with potential US approval in Q2 2026. Self-pay pricing is set at $149-399 per month, significantly below injectable competitors.

entries.summary: Boehringer Ingelheim's survodutide, a glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist, is in Phase 3 across three major programs (SYNCHRONIZE for obesity, LIVERAGE for MASH) with FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation for liver fibrosis.
entries.content: Survodutide is advancing through a comprehensive Phase 3 program spanning obesity (SYNCHRONIZE-1 and SYNCHRONIZE-2), cardiovascular outcomes (SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT with 5,508 participants), and MASH/liver fibrosis (LIVERAGE, with FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation). Phase 2 data showed up to 19% weight loss at 46 weeks and significant liver fat reduction, positioning the glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist as potentially superior for MASH patients. However, tolerability remains a concern with 25% discontinuation rates at the highest dose due to gastrointestinal side effects. Full Phase 3 efficacy results from SYNCHRONIZE are anticipated in 2026, with modified dosing strategies being explored to address tolerability.

entries.summary: CagriSema's REDEFINE 1 Phase 3 results showed 22.7% weight loss (idealized estimand) but fell short of the anticipated 25% target, while Novo Nordisk filed the NDA with FDA in Q1 2026.
entries.content: CagriSema's Phase 3 REDEFINE 1 trial in 3,417 adults showed 22.7% mean weight reduction using the idealized estimand (20.4% treatment-policy estimand) at 68 weeks, with 34.7% of patients achieving 25% or greater weight loss. While clinically significant, the result fell short of the anticipated 25% target that analysts had set, causing market skepticism. REDEFINE 2 in patients with type 2 diabetes showed 13.7% weight loss and 73.5% achieving HbA1c of 6.5% or below. Novo Nordisk filed the NDA with FDA in Q1 2026, with potential approval in late 2026 or early 2027. Only 57.3% of patients reached the highest dose by trial end, suggesting the flexible dosing protocol may have limited peak efficacy.

entries.summary: Retatrutide's Phase 3 TRIUMPH-4 trial delivered record-breaking 28.7% weight loss (on-treatment) at 68 weeks, alongside 75% pain reduction in knee osteoarthritis patients, though 18.2% discontinued due to adverse events at the high dose.
entries.content: Eli Lilly's retatrutide, the first-in-class GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, delivered unprecedented Phase 3 results in TRIUMPH-4: 28.7% weight loss on-treatment (23.7% treatment-regimen) at 68 weeks with the 12mg dose, along with approximately 75% pain reduction in knee osteoarthritis patients. The March 2026 TRANSCEND-T2D-1 results showed 16.8% weight loss and 2.0% HbA1c reduction in type 2 diabetes. However, 18.2% discontinued the high dose due to adverse events (nausea 43.2%, diarrhea 33.1%). With seven more Phase 3 readouts expected in 2026 across obesity, sleep apnea, chronic low back pain, and liver disease, analysts forecast a 2027 approval with $15.6 billion in 2031 sales.

entries.summary: Novo Nordisk's amycretin, a GLP-1/amylin dual agonist available in both injectable and oral forms, showed 14.5% weight loss (subcutaneous) and 10.1% (oral) at 36 weeks in Phase 2, advancing to Phase 3 in 2026.
entries.content: Novo Nordisk's amycretin demonstrated strong Phase 2 results in type 2 diabetes: the subcutaneous formulation achieved 14.5% weight loss and 1.8% HbA1c reduction at 36 weeks, while the oral formulation delivered 10.1% weight loss and 1.5% HbA1c reduction. Weight loss had not yet plateaued at higher doses, suggesting greater efficacy in longer trials. The company is advancing both formulations into Phase 3 for obesity and type 2 diabetes in 2026 across multiple indications. Amycretin's oral formulation is particularly significant as it could offer an alternative to Eli Lilly's orforglipron in the emerging oral GLP-1 market, with Novo positioning it as a potential best-in-class therapy.

entries.summary: Eli Lilly's retatrutide met primary endpoints in a Phase 3 Type 2 diabetes trial (March 2026): 12mg dose reduced HbA1c by 1.9 percentage points from a baseline of 7.9% at 40 weeks, while also delivering 15% weight loss at the 12mg dose. Weight loss had not plateaued, suggesting continued improvement with longer treatment.
entries.content: Eli Lilly's retatrutide (GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist) demonstrated successful Phase 3 results in a new Type 2 diabetes trial reported in March 2026. The 40-week trial enrolled patients with T2DM at a baseline HbA1c of 7.9%. Results: the 12mg dose reduced HbA1c by an average 1.9 percentage points; the 9mg and 4mg groups achieved 1.9% and 1.8% reductions respectively. On weight loss, the 12mg group lost on average 15% of body weight, the 9mg group 14%, and the 4mg group 12% — all substantially better than placebo at 3%. Crucially, weight loss had not plateaued, suggesting results would improve with extended treatment. This builds on the TRIUMPH-4 Phase 3 results (28.7% weight loss in obesity with knee osteoarthritis). Lilly expects to submit a regulatory application for retatrutide in 2026. If approved, retatrutide would represent the first triple-agonist obesity/diabetes drug on the market. GlobalData forecasts retatrutide could generate $15.6 billion in peak sales by 2031. Seven additional Phase 3 readouts are expected through 2026.

entries.summary: Indian companies including Biocon, Sun Pharma, and Dr. Reddy's are developing biosimilar tirzepatide candidates, though approved products are not expected before 2027 due to patent protection extending to 2036 and significant technical manufacturing hurdles.
entries.content: Multiple Indian pharmaceutical companies are building biosimilar tirzepatide pipelines: Biocon, Sun Pharma, Dr. Reddy's, Zydus, and Gland Pharma are at various stages of development. Sun Pharma is additionally developing a dual-target drug to compete directly with tirzepatide's mechanism. However, tirzepatide patents extend to at least 2036 in the US, and approved biosimilar products are unlikely before 2027 even in India. Key challenges include the technical complexity of manufacturing large peptide biologics requiring precise protein folding and analytical characterization, cold-chain logistics, and potential patent litigation from Eli Lilly. Indian CDMOs like Gland Pharma and Concord Biotech (OneSource) could play critical roles as contract manufacturers for the global market.
